newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Jittery market awaits CPI.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Jittery market awaits CPI.

text.p: The March Consumer Price Index (CPI) is expected to be the dominant trading factor in the U.S. financial markets on Tuesday, analysts said.
Economists offered an average forecast of up 0.2 percent for the March CPI, according to a Reuters poll, after a 0.3 percent rise in February.
What the market could find more disturbing is a 0.3 percent or 0.4 percent rise in the core CPI, the index without its more volatile food and energy components.

Economists said if the core CPI is up more sharply than usual, it will be due mainly to three factors. The first is a rise in airfares tied to the March reinstatement of an airline excise tax that had been taken off in January. Hotels also raised room rates in March, economists said. And an "early" Easter may have helped to boost clothing prices, they said.
The reason even a modest surge in the CPI could alarm the market is that it would be happening when the economy is still strong, economists said.

"The one thing to keep in mind is that through this period of strong growth, the one comfort the market has had is that inflation news has been good," said Joshua Feinman, vice president and global markets economist at Bankers Trust.
But if investors become persuaded that the inflation picture has started to deteriorate when the economy is still growing so strongly, bonds would be in trouble, Feinman said.
A rising CPI would be "more threatening than signs of strong economic growth," said Edward Yardeni, managing director and chief economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The reason a rising CPI could prove troublesome is that prices already reflect investors' awareness that the economy is strong, Yardeni said. But a rising inflation trend is not reflected in current prices and if such a picture emerged, prices would have to adjust to reflect that, economists said.
"It's known that the economy is strong, but so far, evidence of an inflation pickup has been pretty scarce," said Yardeni.
Yardeni said the reinstatement of the excise tax on airline fares in March would probably be the biggest contributor to the "outsize increase" in the core CPI.
Knowing that, the market could take a 0.3 percent of 0.4 percent increase in the core CPI in stride, he said. But that is not a certainty.
"The financial markets are so skittish," Yardeni said. "They put a pretty negative spin on things."
The market will also get two private reports on U.S. chain store sales for the week ended April 12.
And the government will report on February business inventories which are expected to be up 0.2 percent after rising 0.1 percent in February.
Business inventories do not typically move the market.
In late trade on Monday, the 30-year Treasury bond was down 1/32 to 93-10/32, yielding 7.17 percent.
Dealers said Fed funds will likely open between 5-9/16 and 5-11/16 percent on Tuesday.
